terms.gloss: next year, a year from now
evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.92: faciendum est ad annum
terms.comment: “For the coming year, a year hence” (Lewis & Short); unlike proximō annō, it cannot mean last year.
With verbs of putting off, wishing or choosing.
proximus is the nearest year either way: Pliny’s proximō annō (Ep. 10.5.1) is last year.

phrases.latin: Furnium nostrum quem ad annum tribūnum pl. vidēbam fore
phrases.english: our friend Furnius, who I could see would be tribune next year

phrases.latin: optāmus enim tibi ōmināmurque in proximum annum cōnsulātum
phrases.english: for we wish you, and foresee for you, the consulship next year

sources: Lewis & Short: annus · Lewis & Short: proximus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 89.
